doc.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019

title: Going to school on the road instead of conservatory
summary: Chez took classes at Rutgers but learned by gigging and listening to other players.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now most high school students who are serious about music they now go the Berklee/ Manhattan School, they go that route. Did you not have to do that, or choose not to?

I kind of worked my way through it. You know? I took classes at Rutgers University. I teach at the University of Virginia, which is a great school. But I chose to go to school on the road. I went to school gigging, doing different gigs and playing with different guys. And man I’m always listening. There’s guys that are teaching and I’m in the corner listening and I’m picking up what they’re saying you know. There’s guys that are practicing you know and trumpet player wars they call it. You know? You’re warming up and there’s a guy playing and another guy oh yeah? You know what I’m talking about, right? Not me. I’m listening to what that guy’s playing because I’m going to learn. Again, the smartest man in the world doesn’t know everything. So there’s always room to learn, there’s always room to pick up. You know when you start – when you stop honing your craft you’re done. And I ain’t done.
